newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian protesters stone ruling party HQ.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian protesters stone ruling party HQ.

text.p: Opposition protesters calling for early elections hurled stones at the headquarters of the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party in Sofia on Friday.
They also threw firecrackers at police and broke two windows in the Pozitano Street office building. Riot police with helmets and shields deployed around the building.
"In the name of Bulgaria, in the name of our future and our children, we demand early elections," Ivan Kostov, leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces, told the crowd.

Protesters, estimated by witnesses at more than 10,000, marched from the National Palace of Culture carrying banners reading "Communists ruined the country" and "Let's get rid of the Communist terror".
The Socialist party was formed by leading Communists after the collapse of one-party rule in 1989.
Prime minister and party leader Zhan Videnov resigned on December 21 after severe criticism of his management of the economy.
A new Socialist cabinet is expected to be formed by mid-January but the opposition wants elections due in December 1998 to be brought forward.
